A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NIGHTJAR/shared-program-state research. Their main text, figures, tables, formal definitions, and Appendices A-G are readable and comparable, including the reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on SPSBench, graph queries, and GSM8K, including runtime measurements, ablations, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The shared scopes, heap, control-state interface, Python specialization, eager variable loading, and caching procedures are retained. Renaming natural code as prompts does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 25 SPSBench programs, graph-query and graph-scaling scenarios, and full 1,319-problem GSM8K evaluation. Appendix reordering introduces no additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the manual implementations, code-interpreter comparators, NIGHTJAR variants, and LLM code-generation baseline. Table 8 retains both OpenAI and custom code-interpreter comparisons on GSM8K.

E3.justification: Models, metrics, main temperature setting, 300-call limit, 1,000-second timeout, and appendix evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The explicit 25-node description in v2 clarifies the existing example rather than documenting a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The implementation ablations, temperature-zero evaluation, smaller-model evaluation, graph-scaling study, effects/runtime analysis, and failure analyses are retained. Additional evaluation results move from Appendix D to E.

E5.justification: Both retain five-run reporting for the principal evaluations, three runs for GSM8K, standard deviations, runtime ranges, and the same 125-run failure-analysis summaries. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted data are unchanged, but Section 6 newly asserts that NIGHTJAR (Baseline) is slower than Manual Implementation (Code Interpreter). Table 2 supports this for Sonnet 4 (55.6 versus 36.8 seconds), but contradicts it for GPT-4.1 (39.0 versus 50.3 seconds).

T1.justification: The formal syntax, effects, handlers, and operational semantics in Figures 3-7 and Appendix B are unchanged apart from terminology. The host-language assumptions are restated in Section 4.2 rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The central abstraction, interface contributions, and accuracy/code-length claims remain. The revised introduction and new Section 8 broaden the implications toward adaptive computing and systems remaining robust under changing contexts without extensive manual engineering.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explanation attributing baseline runtime to attempts to work around unsupported tasks. Section 5.2 additionally names high-level control-flow constructs among generic-interface limitations. Existing nondeterminism qualifications remain in Appendix E.4.

D1.justification: Figure 1 and Section 3.1 change the documented embedded-block identifier from natural to prompt, and Section 3.3 explicitly identifies the example graph as having 25 nodes. System prompts, hardware information, model identifiers, and repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and comparisons with isolated or partially shared state systems remain substantively unchanged. Reference changes update publication information, titles, capitalization, and venue names for the same works.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten around prompts and programs instead of natural and formal code. Explanatory transitions are revised, limitations and conclusion become separate sections, and the system-prompt and evaluation appendices exchange positions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 rearranges its manual implementation, NIGHTJAR, and console panels and expands the caption. Figure 2 moves and receives terminology updates; appendix displays are relocated and conference headers added. The experimental display designs are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 offers clearer figure explanations and more explicit document organization. However, it introduces a runtime generalization contradicted by part of Table 2 and broader robustness claims without additional supporting evaluation. These presentation gains and losses in claim precision leave the net quality direction uncertain.
